Issued at 1200 AM CDT Thu Sep 3 2026

This Morning - Overnight: Uncertain Storm Chances and Severe 
Potential 

A very complex forecast is in store for our area over the next 24 
hours as hi-res guidance continues to struggle with how to capture 
potential convective evolution this morning and into the evening. 
Currently, confidence is increasing for storms to develop across the 
region during the morning hours as an axis of 850mb moisture 
transport and sfc theta-e advection overrides a quasi-stationary 
boundary across the region. Consequently, expecting showers and 
storms to quickly increase in coverage and push northeast with this 
forcing regime. Overall, the environment for this morning convection 
is not overly impressive as the nocturnal inversion will be firmly 
in place as convection is ongoing which should trend more elevated 
in nature. However, cannot rule out some large hail with stronger 
cores as both elongated hodographs in the recent RAP and modest mid-
level lapse rates of 6.5-7 C/km are present during the morning.

The key question will be exactly how long morning convection will 
linger across the area and if it will inhibit the potential for 
convection during the evening and into the overnight. Currently, 00z 
CAMs have generally shifted towards a more limited convective 
scenario which would suggest morning convection staying present 
across the local area later into the morning, perhaps even early 
afternoon. If this is the case, destabilization would be limited in 
nature and a shortwave impulse that would be responsible for 
organizing a potential MCS later into the evening would not have 
much instability to work with. However, in the event that 
destabilization does occur, ample instability and somewhat favorable 
shear profiles would allow for robust cold pool organization and a 
subsequent damaging wind risk. Another scenario that some of the 
recent 00z CAMs have also picked up on is a pronounced 850mb 
moisture transport axis later into the overnight interacting with 
the aforementioned quasi-stationary boundary. This coupled with any 
lingering instability would be enough for convective development to 
occur in a focused corridor leading to the potential for training 
storms which is currently depicted in the 00z HRRR. Cannot rule out 
some heavy rain potential if this scenario pans out given warm 
cloud depths in excess of 4km and precipitable waters over 1.75". 

In all, there appears to be multiple scenarios for this 
evening/overnight, all of which are fairly low confidence at this 
point. Confidence will likely increase in light of morning 
convective trends. The main takeaways from guidance at this point is 
that some severe potential is in play and that the MCS scenario 
later into the is fairly low confidence but could have some 
potential for higher wind gusts (over 70 mph) if it manifests. 

Friday: Shower & Storm Chances, Low-End Severe Potential 

The pattern for Friday really does not change all that much with 
there being some question with how prior storm activity may affect 
any potential for storms on Friday. However, given fairly robust 
instability profiles with MLCAPE values approaching 4000 J/kg could 
suggest substantial buoyancy for quick developing updrafts. This 
coupled with robust DCAPE values in the RAP would suggest any 
collapsing cores could have a damaging wind gust risk and perhaps 
some large hail with mid-level lapse rates hovering around 6.5C/km. 
However, given the fairly unimpressive shear profiles with minimal 
hodographs elongation, thinking that any updrafts that do get going 
would be short-lived. 

Holiday Weekend & Early Next Week: Persisting Shower and Storm 
Chances 

As we head into the weekend and early next week, upper-level ridging 
remains to our west with the local area subjected to a northwesterly 
flow regime. Consequently, additional shortwave impulses may move 
into the region this weekend and early next week. Overall the grand 
ensemble (GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) has respectable probabilities 
(40-60%) for measurable precipitation throughout the weekend and 
into early next week, so thinking off and on storm chances are 
feasible. As far as any severe potential, AI/ML guidance highlights 
some low-end potential (5% chance) over the weekend, however likely 
any severe potential would be dictated by mesoscale factors so would 
be challenging to hone in on any definitive severe potential at this 
point.
